::: {.lead}
Today you use Office in more than one place, and you move work between
apps. Each experiment has two parts. **Part A** is in Office on the lab
computer. **Part B** is on a simulator of the interactive lesson: on paper,
scan its QR code; on the screen, click its link. After each step, write
your result in its box. At the end, copy your key results into the table.
:::

## Before you start

- **You need:** a lab computer with Excel and Word, a browser and your
  university account.
- **No lab computer today?** Do Part B of each experiment on your phone. Do
  Part A later on any computer, with Office on the web at `office.com`.
- **Check:** the results are at the end of this worksheet. Look only after
  you try. On the interactive lesson, every step has a check that answers
  at once.

## Experiment 1 · One file, three places, and a PDF copy

**The idea:** one Office file opens in three places. The **desktop app**
has all the features. **Office on the web** (`office.com`) needs no install,
and AutoSave is always on there. The **phone app** has the main features.
A **PDF** copy keeps the look, and people do not easily change it; the
`.docx` file stays.

**Aim:** write in Word on the web, and make a PDF copy there.

::: {.part}
**Part A · In the app (Word on the web)**
:::

1. Open `office.com`, sign in, open **Word** and choose **Blank document**.
   Type: *The computer club meets on Monday at 1 p.m. in room 12.* Look at
   the top of the window, next to the name of the file.

   {{< record "Next to the name, it says" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **Saved** (or **Saved to OneDrive**). On the web, AutoSave is always on:
   every change goes to OneDrive at once, so there is no Save button to
   press.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   You type in Word on the web. Why do you not press Save?

   - [x] AutoSave is always on, on the web: the file saves itself in OneDrive.

     Why: On the web, every change goes to OneDrive at once.

   - [ ] Word on the web does not keep files.

     Why: It keeps them in OneDrive.

   - [ ] The file is saved only when you close the browser.

     Why: It is saved after every change, while you type.
   :::

2. Click **File › Export › Download as PDF**, then **Download**. Open the
   PDF from the downloads of the browser.

   {{< record "Where the PDF is … ; is the Word file still in OneDrive?" lines=2 >}}

   ::: {.check}
   The PDF is in the **Downloads** folder of the browser. The Word document
   is **still in OneDrive**: the PDF is a second file, a copy for reading
   and printing.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   Word on the web made a PDF copy of your note. Which is true?

   - [x] You have two files: the `.docx` in OneDrive and the `.pdf` copy.

     Why: A PDF copy is a second file; the Word file stays.

   - [ ] The `.docx` file became a `.pdf` file.

     Why: Making a PDF copy never changes the Word file.

   - [ ] You can change the PDF like the `.docx`.

     Why: A PDF is for reading and printing: people do not easily change it.
   :::

::: {.part}
**Part B · On the simulator** (no computer? do it on your phone)
:::

{{< sim file="../../week-03/sims/pdf-export.html" poster="../../week-03/sims/pdf-export.png" title="PDF Export: one file, three places" >}}

3. In **PDF Export**, make the PDF copy of `notice.docx` in the three
   places: the desktop app, the web and the phone. Which way does the
   desktop app use?

   {{< record "Desktop app: … › … › … › …" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **File › Save As › PDF (\*.pdf) › Save** (or File › Export › Create
   PDF/XPS Document › Publish). On the web: File › Export › Download as
   PDF. On the phone: … › Export › PDF.
   :::

   ::: {.order}
   Put the clicks in order: a PDF copy in the desktop app of Word.

   1. File
   2. Save As
   3. PDF (\*.pdf)
   4. Save

   Why: In the desktop app, Save As can change the type to PDF; the .docx stays.
   :::

## Experiment 2 · Copy a table from Excel to Word

**The idea:** **Ctrl + C** puts the table on the **clipboard**, until you
paste it. When you paste it into Word, the small **Paste Options** button
gives four ways: **Keep Source Formatting** (the Excel look), **Use
Destination Styles** (the look of your document; you can still change it),
**Picture** (an image: nobody can change the numbers) and **Keep Text
Only** (no table lines).

**Aim:** paste one table in two ways, and see what you can change.

::: {.part}
**Part A · In the apps (Excel and Word)**
:::

1. In Excel, open a **Blank workbook** and type in A1:B4: **Day, Visitors**;
   **Sunday, 40**; **Monday, 35**; **Tuesday, 50**. Select A1:B4 and press
   **Ctrl + C**. Open a new Word document and press **Ctrl + V**. Click the
   **Paste Options** button (Ctrl) under the table and choose **Use
   Destination Styles**. Then change 35 to **45**.

   {{< record "Could I change the number? … ; the look is …" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **Yes**: the table is a Word table now, with the look of your document,
   and you changed Monday to 45 in Word.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   You pasted the table with **Use Destination Styles**. Which is true?

   - [x] It has the look of the document, and you can still change the numbers.

     Why: It is a Word table now, with the styles of your document.

   - [ ] It is a picture: nobody can change the numbers.

     Why: That is the Picture option.

   - [ ] It has no table lines.

     Why: That is Keep Text Only.
   :::

2. Click under the table, and press **Ctrl + V** again. This time choose
   **Picture**. Click on a number of the new table and try to change it.

   {{< record "Can I change a number in the picture? …" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **No.** Picture pastes an image of the table: nobody can change the
   numbers by mistake. To change them, change the table in Excel and copy
   it again.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   You pasted the table as a **Picture**. Monday must be 55, not 45. What
   do you do?

   - [x] Change it in Excel, copy the table again and paste it again.

     Why: A picture is an image: you cannot type in it.

   - [ ] Click the number in the picture and type 55.

     Why: You cannot change the numbers of a picture.

   - [ ] Press Ctrl + S: the picture updates.

     Why: Saving does not change what the picture shows.
   :::

::: {.part}
**Part B · On the simulator** (no computer? do it on your phone)
:::

{{< sim file="../../week-03/sims/paste-lab.html" poster="../../week-03/sims/paste-lab.png" title="Paste Lab: from Excel to Word" >}}

3. In **Paste Lab**, do the four tasks: choose the right Paste Option for
   each one. Which option keeps the green heading of the Excel table?

   {{< record "The green heading stays with …" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **Keep Source Formatting**: it keeps the look of the Excel table. Use
   Destination Styles takes the look of the Word report, Picture makes an
   image, and Keep Text Only drops the table lines.
   :::

   ::: {.sort}
   After you paste, can you still change the numbers? Sort the four options.

   Yes, you can change them
   :   Keep Source Formatting

       Why: It is a Word table with the Excel look.

   :   Use Destination Styles

       Why: It is a Word table with the look of your document.

   :   Keep Text Only

       Why: The words and numbers are text that you can change.

   No, you cannot change them
   :   Picture

       Why: A picture is an image of the table.
   :::

## Experiment 3 · Share a file safely

**The idea:** **Share** makes a link to a file in OneDrive. You choose
**who** can open the link (Anyone with the link, People in your
organization, or Specific people) and **what** they can do (**Can view** or
**Can edit**). Share only with the people who need the file, and give Can
edit only to people who must change it.

**Aim:** read the settings of a share link, and choose safe ones.

::: {.part}
**Part A · In the app (OneDrive)**
:::

1. In OneDrive (from `office.com`), find the document of Experiment 1.
   Select it and click **Share**, then open the link settings. Choose
   **People in your organization** and **Can view**. Do **not** send the
   link: close the window.

   {{< record "Who can open it … ; what they can do …" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **People in your organization**: only people with a university account
   can open the link. **Can view**: they read the file, but they cannot
   change it.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   Who can open a link with **People in your organization**?

   - [x] only people with a university account

     Why: The organization is the university: nobody from outside opens it.

   - [ ] anyone who gets the link

     Why: That is "Anyone with the link".

   - [ ] only the people whose names you type

     Why: That is "Specific people".
   :::

::: {.part}
**Part B · On the simulator** (no computer? do it on your phone)
:::

{{< sim file="../../week-03/sims/share-settings.html" poster="../../week-03/sims/share-settings.png" title="Share Settings: who and what?" >}}

2. In **Share Settings**, choose who and what for each of the four files.
   Which file gets **Anyone with the link**?

   {{< record "Anyone with the link: the file …" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **price-list.pdf**: every customer who gets the link may read it (Can
   view). The class report goes only to Ms Rana, the group presentation
   only to Sami (Can edit), and the club notes stay in the university.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   In Share Settings, which file may people from outside the university
   open?

   - [x] price-list.pdf, for every customer with the link

     Why: Anyone with the link, Can view: customers read the prices.

   - [ ] club-notes.docx

     Why: Only students and staff of the university may read the club notes.

   - [ ] class-report.docx

     Why: Only the teacher, Ms Rana, gets this link.
   :::
